standard_prerequisites.name: Symmetric interval exchange transformation
standard_prerequisites.statement: An IET is symmetric when the reflection of the interval conjugates it to its inverse off the discontinuities.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis and the source of the conjugacy identity.

standard_prerequisites.name: Reflection centres
standard_prerequisites.statement: c_alpha denotes the centre of the subinterval indexed by alpha, and c_{1/2} is the centre of the whole interval.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the points whose backward iterates are computed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Generalised conjugacy identity
standard_prerequisites.statement: The reflection applied to the n-th iterate equals the minus-n-th iterate of the reflection, off the relevant discontinuities.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the identity applied in the proof.

core_obligations: Argue that the hypothesis that the first m iterates of c_alpha avoid the endpoints makes all the points appearing in the computation points of continuity of the reflection and of its inverse (source line 532).

Apply the generalised conjugacy identity with the appropriate exponent, distinguishing the case alpha equal to one half, where the reflection fixes the centre, from the other case, where the reflection sends the centre to its first iterate (source lines 535-544 and 548).
Collect the two cases into the displayed formula with the indicator delta_{1/2} (source lines 535-544).

proof_roadmap.step: Use the hypothesis on the iterates to stay at points of continuity.
Apply the conjugacy identity with the exponent corrected by the indicator of the case alpha equal to one half.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 530-545: under the assumption that the first m iterates of a centre avoid the endpoints, the minus-m-th iterate of that centre is obtained by applying the reflection to a shifted iterate, the shift being given by the indicator of the case where the index is one half. The proof (source lines 547-549) is short but it depends on two observations that the statement does not contain: the hypothesis is exactly what makes the points of the computation points of continuity of the reflection and of its inverse, and the case distinction between the centre of the whole interval, which the reflection fixes, and the other centres, which the reflection sends to their first iterate, is what produces the indicator in the formula.
